transcript: Dylan Mulvaney show is one of my favorite shows I saw the entire time I was at friend. I think it's because she immediately invites you into her story. Like, literally, as soon as you walk into this space, you see Dylan dressed in this stunning outfit. She's talking to everyone, she's giving hugs. She's just so warm and effervescent and makes you feel like you are invited to be there. And this is a deeply personal story. It's a story of Dylan's life and her transition, all of the beauty and all of the challenges that have come along with that. But it never feels dark or heavy. It really manages to skate this incredibly beautiful, fine line of going through the hard parts of Dylan Story but keeping it very joyful and humorous and silly. The set is perfect. It's really cleverly staged. I loved all of the costumes, and there is some audience participation, which sometimes I don't love, but in this case, it's so beautifully utilized. Like, truly one of my favorite moments. And it's so much a testament to both the performer that Dylan is, her vulnerability, her ability to connect with an audience where you will follow her literally anywhere, and also the direction by Tim Jackson. I think even if you've been following Dylan for a long time and you know her story, getting to hear her tell it herself is so special. If I have any notes that at one point the Show transitions into a musical and I just want more music. Dylan is just such a great show woman, and I want more of that. You want to see Dylan? Show? It's at Assembly George Square Studios. Follow along for more videos on my favorite fringe shows.
